newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil attracts more direct investment - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil attracts more direct investment - paper.

text.p: Brazilian Central Bank figures show the type of foreign capital entering the country is improving on the back of economic stability, O Globo newspaper reported.
Short term speculative capital invested in the financial markets has fallen to $4.3 billion in the first nine months of this year from $16.5 billion in the same period last year, the newspaper said.

Meanwhile, direct investment by multinational companies has increased to $6.6 billion in the first nine months of 1996, and the Central Bank expects this figure to jump to $8 billion by December and to $10 billion in 1997, O Globo said. Last year, foreign direct investment reached $3.9 billion.
The privatization of state-owned companies such as power distributor Light and sections of the federal railway network contributed to the rise in direct investment.

Investments by multinationals to increase production capacity of their Brazilian subsidiaries brought $1.3 billion in direct investment, while the fusion or acquisition of companies and banks brought another $960 million, O Globo said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
